title: alectra rigida subsp. paludosa
intro: Alectra rigida subsp. paludosa, commonly known as marsh violet, is a plant species in the family Orobanchaceae. It is a parasitic plant that obtains its nutrients by connecting to the roots of surrounding plants, typically grasses and wildflowers. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, which include the treatment of fever, rheumatism, and digestive issues. The bioactive constituents of Alectra rigida subsp. paludosa include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and alkaloids, which are believed to contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects.
